messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: page fired for service=runtime-text-gen region=eu-west metric=p99_latency value=1620ms threshold=1200ms link=<https://pd.company/INC-17512|INC-17512>

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-17512 created, page sent to on-call schedule.

Ben: Acked on PD, jumping in. Can someone confirm customer impact?

Maya: Not seeing 5xxs in frontend, but a handful of customers reporting slow completions (timeouts at app-level). DM'd product leads.

Sam: Looking at runtime metrics now — GPU queues spiking and KV cache eviction rate up ~12x over baseline since 02:10 UTC. Putting quick query: ``curl https://metrics-api/series?service=runtime-text-gen&metric=kv_evictions`` — results look like a sharp clamp during last deploy.

Priya: Deploy? We rolled a small scheduler change at 02:05 UTC to tweak batch sizing. Could be causing churn. Will check rollout group.

Ben: If kv evictions are thrashing, p99 will skyrocket. Can we scale autoscaler aggressively while we triage? I can run an emergency scale.

Priya: Go ahead, scaling worker pool from 3 -> 8 across eu-west pools. Command:
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment runtime-text-gen-workers --replicas=8 --context=cluster-eu-west
```

Ben: Running that now. ``kubectl exec -n infra deploy/ops-runner -- bash -c 'kubectl scale deployment runtime-text-gen-workers --replicas=8 --context=cluster-eu-west'``

incident-bot: Autoscaling action started (initiated by Ben). Scaling deployments to 8 replicas.

Sam: While that rolls, I'm temporarily toggling the kvcache sticky eviction policy to reduce thrash: ``POST /admin/kvcache/config {"eviction_jitter": true, "warmup_seconds": 60}`` — applying now.

Ben: Noted. Also putting a soft routing fallback to model-variant-small for heavy customers to reduce per-token latency. Updating route policy: ``redwood route update --service runtime-text-gen --fallback model-small --effect now``

pagerduty-bot: INC-17512 acknowledged by Ben at 02:18 UTC.

Alice: Taking over handoff in 10m — Ben, do you want a full runbook writeup or quick postmortem?

Ben: Quick: scale + kvcache tweak + fallback to small model reduced p99 from 1620ms -> ~680ms within ~6 minutes. I'll leave timeline + commands in the incident doc, Alice please continue monitoring and file follow-up for rollout gating.

Sam: Metrics look healthy — GPU queue length dropping, kv eviction rate back near baseline. P99 trending down: 1200 -> 720 -> 680ms. No customer errors observed after fallback.

Maya: Communicated interim status to CS and flagged for customer success follow-up for the few slow reports.

Alice: Ack and taking lead. I'll keep PD open for 15m of stable p99 then close. Creating follow-up ticket to add eviction threshold to rollout checks.

Ben: Thanks team. Follow-ups: (1) add kvcache eviction monitor to rollout gate, (2) add autoscale override runbook snippet, (3) evaluate batch-size change in staging.

pagerduty-bot: INC-17512 status changed: monitoring.

incident-bot: Note added by Ben: "Immediate mitigation = scale out + kvcache jitter + fallback to model-small. Suspect scheduler batch-size change triggered eviction thrash. Postmortem required."

Alice: Will close PD after 15m stable. Adding owners and ETA for postmortem to the ticket. :handshake:

Ben: Leaving oncall to Alice, backfilling in rotation. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Alice: Closing notes: p99 stabilized at ~660ms after final adjustments. Follow-up ticket: RW-3721 (runbook + rollout gate).
